Write down your seed

These twelve words are your wallet. Anyone with them controls your Bitcoin. Anyone without them cannot access it — not Plotzwerks, not anyone.

Write them on paper. Store the paper somewhere safe. Consider a stainless steel backup — fire and water proof. Stay offline, don't screenshot, don't email, don't type them into anything but a new wallet, Lightning or onchain, if you ever need to recover.

WATCH-ONLY EXPORT · account zpub
Build a watch-only coordinator (Sparrow, BlueWallet, Electrum) without ever typing the 12 words: reveal, then scan or copy. A zpub can see balances and build unsigned transactions — it can never spend.
ESCAPE KIT · if the LSP disappears
Exit lightning and collect your onchain and lightning balances. Two pieces of text per channel, already signed, no secrets: THE CLOSE ends the channel on the Bitcoin network; THE COLLECT moves your share to your own address after the shown wait. Paste each artifact from the CLOSING and OPEN cards in turn on any online explorer’s broadcast page — settled channels have nothing left to collect — and never return to this wallet.
Export only from the phone you most recently used — an escape kit from an old backup is out of date, and broadcasting old state can forfeit your balance under Lightning’s anti-cheat rules. Broadcasting THE COLLECT early is harmless: the network refuses it until the wait is over, so just try again later.

Recovery Phrase
Inside the Lightning LIJOX standard…
if you lose or erase your device: your 12 words + your encrypted channel-state backup bring back everything — channels included.
if you have only your 12 words: channels close on device open, and your money returns on-chain within a few confirmations.
if you never open LIJOX again: your LSP closes your channels on its timer, and every sat arrives at your seed on-chain.
if your LSP is gone and your backup with it: your escape kit closes the channels without the LSP — find it below, and in the offline room. Keeping a copy where only your 12 words can find it is in build.
Outside LIJOX
your on-chain sats sit at standard BIP84 paths. In any other wallet (BlueWallet, Sparrow, Electrum), set its gap limit to 500 first — LiJ spreads addresses farther than default scans look.
No one — not even your LSP — can redirect a single sat.

Dials
User-adjustable settings
Auto-lock
Locks the wallet behind the passphrase after the app has been hidden this long. Never means it stays open until you close it.
Updates
Automatic takes each new build the next time you open the wallet online. Ask me keeps the build you have running until you tap Update on a card that shows the new versions and the engine’s hashes. Neither can stop a hostile update from the site itself — the browser replaces the wallet from its origin, so a malicious build could ignore this setting. What Ask me gives you: no silent replacement, and a chance to check the engine hashes against the published build before it runs.
Speed up slow closes
A cooperative close can sit unconfirmed when fees rise after it was signed. Speeding it up spends its output back to you with a small extra fee that pulls it into a block (a child-pays-for-parent transaction). Off: you decide each time, from the on-chain row’s Speed up button, which shows the fee first. Automatic: the wallet does it by itself once the close has waited three blocks and the network rate is well above what the close pays.
Send
Fee race margin
Sats MAX leaves unfilled in case the network fee moves between the quote and your tap. Zero is exact \u2014 and if a zero-margin MAX ever bounces, the wallet quietly steps down and retries to the sat.
Receive
LNURL Receive code settings
Your printable QR and address · enable under Privacy → LSP
LSP Honesty Reserve
What your LSP counterparty must reserve before you accept payments from their side — yours to set. Lower amounts lets you access receive room sooner — but weakens your take-back protection vs. the LSP while your phone is off. New channels only — channels you already have keep the reserve they opened with.
Display currencyUSD
What the balance long-press and every fiat readout show. Rates come from your LSP; a code it does not quote is refused.
Privacy
LSP
What the LSP sees
What you must share to get routing at all: your invoices, amounts, timing, channel balances, and IP — the LSP is your channel counterparty and sees the traffic it carries. What it never holds: your keys or your funds.
Payment holding
The LSP can hold an incoming payment while you’re away — a longer window means more it observes; Off means offline payments fail fast instead. Your choice is sent to the LSP and clamped to its ceiling. This dial governs regular bolt11 invoices (amount receives) — LNURL address receives ride their own network-fixed window instead.
Wake push
When a Lightning payment is waiting and LiJ is closed, your LSP sends a silent nudge so your phone shows a “payment waiting” notification. Tap it to reopen LiJ and the payment lands — no amount or detail travels with it, just a wake.
Wake this phone
Telemetry
Session logs live in memory only — the last 400 lines — and vanish when the wallet closes. Close-tapes rest on this device in plain storage, newest three kept, older pruned automatically. Off means nothing ever leaves this device; on ships both to the LSP when the wallet hides — and the LSP stops expecting on its own when you go quiet.
Ship device logs
LSP ping frequency
An open wallet polls the LSP continuously — it knows when you’re here. Quiet checks in about every ten seconds instead: payments still work, they land a beat slower, and your presence pattern blurs.
Quiet
Static address
On: with no amount entered, Receive shows your static address — reusable, no expiry, held non-custodially by your LSP until you return. Off: every receive is a one-time bolt11 invoice and the address stays paused; claims already registered with your LSP remain payable until they run out. A permanent public code: every payer is visible to the LSP, and reuse links your receipts together as the LSP. Rotate severs that link — payers of the old code lose the thread. Old QR may keep receiving at the LSP until the already-submitted pre-signed invoices run out; full server-side removal TBA.
Receive via LNURL
Data retention
What the LSP keeps, and for how long — every LIJOX provider will declare it. Shown here when manifests go live.
Network
Quorum counterparties
Independent operators cross-check the chain so no single one can lie to you. What you share to get this: each sees the addresses and transactions you ask about, and your IP. What they can’t know: your keys, your other addresses, or each other’s answers. The LSP declares the default set; you can add operators of your own on top — never fewer. Left blank, the LSP defaults stand. One healthy endpoint is enough to function; the count colors green when all answer, amber when some do.
Address watcher
When you’re expecting an on-chain payment, LiJ asks this endpoint whether your address has been paid — so it shows before it confirms. The default is the LSP’s own. Point it at your node’s Esplora and 0-conf checks stay fully yours. Saved on this device.
Broadcast routing
All four: a transaction fans out to every explorer at once — most reliable, and all four operators see it each time. One at a time: it goes to a single explorer (rotating per transaction) and stops at the first acceptance. Bitcoin needs just one honest node to propagate either way.
One at a time
Cloud
Encrypted cloud backup
Channel state backs up after every change, sealed under your key before it leaves. What you share to get recovery-without-the-device: Cloudflare (the backup host) sees that an encrypted blob arrived, its size, the timing of your activity, and your IP — never contents, never keys. Off means nothing leaves this device — recovery then depends on this phone surviving. Download saves the same sealed blob to this device as an archival copy; load it back anytime from Maintenance → Load backup from device.
Cloud backup
Registry lookups
Finding an LSP means asking the registry — a Cloudflare-hosted worker. What you share to get discovery: the registry sees your IP and that this wallet is shopping for a provider. It learns nothing about your funds, keys, or channels.
Delegated sats
Delegation chits mint through pageapp.app — a Cloudflare Worker: pageapp and Cloudflare see amounts, timing, and your IP, and the chit’s state lives on Cloudflare’s rails — if those rails go dark, delegation pauses. Keys never leave you: bounded spend authority is what’s delegated, and the payment preimage never touches the server.
Third-party scripts
Zero. Every script ships inside the app — QR tools, scanners, UR codecs, all vendored. No CDN, no analytics, no font server. Nothing outside this device learns the wallet even opened. It's a beautiful thing.
Device
What rests here
Your seed and channels are sealed under the vault. In plain storage, readable if the device is: cached balances, recent activity, and diagnostic tapes (close logs, scan logs — device-only, never shipped). Your zpub appears only while revealed and is never stored. Clearing lives under Maintenance.
Offline start
Open the wallet with no network and still reach what’s yours: Lightning balances decoded live from this device’s channel state, fresh receive addresses, your static pay code, your recovery words and account zpub, offline transaction signing by camera or paste, and Erase. Nothing is shared with anyone — no network, no counterparty. Sending, live receive detection, and prices need the network and will say so.
Start without a network
Encrypt history
Your seed is always encrypted. This seals the payment ledger, close records, and scan logs on this device under a key derived from your seed: a phone thief, a backup extract, or forensics without your passphrase reads only ciphertext. Nothing here leaves the device either way — this row is about whoever picks up the phone. Balance snapshots stay plaintext for instant boot. Flipping the switch takes effect immediately.
Encrypt history
Work in progress
Whirlpool open & close
Coinjoined channel funding and closing. Not yet built.
BOLT12 offers
The reusable pay code that doesn’t link your payments. Not yet built.
Silent payments
Sending to a silent-payment address (sp1q\u2026) works: paste or scan it in Send on-chain and the coins go to a fresh taproot address only the recipient can find (BIP-352). Receiving one for yourself is not built yet.
Your keys live on this device. Your 12-word recovery phrase is the only backup. Lightning in a Jar is non-custodial — no one else holds your funds.

Mutual close
Channel —
Asks the other side to close this channel together. Your funds will move on-chain to an address you can access with a Bitcoin wallet using your seed phrase.
Funds will arrive at
—
If the other side is unresponsive, you can switch to force close at any time during negotiation, which will hold your funds for approximately 24 hours and settle to a different address.
End LSP relationship
—
Mutually close all channels with this provider. Your funds will move on-chain to addresses you can access with a Bitcoin wallet using your seed phrase.
Funds will arrive at
—
After this, your wallet will not be connected to any LSP. You can choose a new provider from the marketplace at any time.
Force close
Channel —
Force-closes this channel without the other side's cooperation. Use this only if mutual close is failing or the other side is unresponsive.
Your funds will be timelocked for ~24 hours
Force close incurs higher on-chain fees and your funds become spendable only after the timelock expires (typically 144 blocks).
Funds will eventually arrive at
—
Because you are the one closing, Lightning's rules make your balance wait: it sits in a timelocked close output for 144 blocks (~24h). When the timer matures, the wallet automatically moves it to your m/84 (BIP84) on-chain address \u2014 from then on it is plain bitcoin, visible to any wallet with your seed. (If the LSP closes instead, your side skips the wait and lands at m/84 immediately.)
